record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: What is the full phase diagram of realistic three-dimensional and bilayer two-orbital manganite models, including whether they host additional competing ordered phases beyond the known A-type antiferromagnetic state near x=0, ferromagnetic metal near x≈0.3, CE-type order near x=0.5, C-type order near x≈0.75, and G-type order near x=1?

evidence.quote: For example, the phase diagram in three dimensions of the two-orbitals model may contain many surprises. ... one can easily imagine a surprisingly rich phase diagram for bilayers or 3D systems. ... However, the details remain unclear.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-orbital double-exchange model for manganites on a three-dimensional cubic lattice and on a bilayer (two coupled square-lattice planes) geometry. The Hamiltonian includes: (i) hopping of e_g electrons between nearest-neighbor Mn sites in the two-orbital basis {d_{x^2-y^2}, d_{3z^2-r^2}} with the standard orbital- and direction-dependent hopping amplitudes; (ii) a large Hund coupling J_H between the e_g spin and a localized t_{2g} core spin S=3/2 (often treated as a classical unit vector); (iii) antiferromagnetic superexchange J_AF between nearest-neighbor t_{2g} spins; (iv) cooperative Jahn–Teller coupling λ between the e_g orbitals and the Q_2, Q_3 lattice distortions, together with their elastic energy; and (v) optionally on-site Hubbard U and inter-orbital U' Coulomb interactions. Let x denote the hole doping (fraction of Mn^{4+}).

Determine the complete ground-state phase diagram of this model as a function of x and the model parameters (J_AF, λ, U, U', bandwidth, and, in the bilayer case, the interlayer coupling). The following ordered phases are already known to appear in appropriate regions: A-type antiferromagnetic order near x=0, ferromagnetic metallic order near x≈0.3, CE-type charge/orbital/spin order near x=0.5, C-type antiferromagnetic order near x≈0.75, and G-type antiferromagnetic order near x=1. The question is to identify all additional competing ordered or inhomogeneous phases (e.g. further charge-, orbital-, spin- or stripe-ordered states, phase-separated regions, or novel orbital liquids) that appear in the full 3D and bilayer phase diagrams, and to delineate the regions of (x, parameter) space where each occurs.
artifact.status_search_result: The full phase diagram of realistic 3D and bilayer two-orbital manganite models is still not completely characterized. Partial results exist (e.g., established A-type, FM, CE, C-type, and G-type regions; CE/A-AF phase competition in bilayer La2-2xSr1+2xMn2O7; bi-stripe orbital order near x≈0.59; nanoscale phase coexistence in La0.25Sr0.75MnO3), but a complete classification of all competing phases across the full doping range and parameter space has not been achieved, with new ordered/phase-separated states continuing to be reported.

status_evidence.title: Localization of electrons due to orbitally ordered bi-stripes in the bilayer manganite La2-2xSr1+2xMn2O7 (x ∼ 0.59)
status_evidence.snippet: Reports novel bi-stripe orbital order in bilayer manganites at intermediate doping, beyond the canonical CE phase.
status_evidence.claim: Additional competing orbital-ordered phases continue to be discovered in bilayer manganites, indicating the phase diagram is not fully classified.

status_evidence.title: Nano scale phase coexistence and charge-ordering with 3dx2-y2 orbital-ordering in La0.25Sr0.75MnO3.01
status_evidence.snippet: Reports nano-scale phase coexistence and novel orbital ordering in 3D manganite near x=0.75.
status_evidence.claim: New competing inhomogeneous and orbital-ordered states beyond the standard list still appear in experimental and theoretical studies.

status_evidence.title: Colossal magnetoresistant materials: the key role of phase separation
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews the rich, incompletely understood phase diagrams and emphasizes phase separation as central, competing physics in manganite models.
status_evidence.claim: The phase diagram of two-orbital manganite models in 3D and bilayer geometries continues to host competing states not yet fully enumerated.
